name: The Weather Prophets
label: Creation Records
lede: Pete Astor went from the Loft's on-stage split straight into a new band, with Alan McGee briefly on bass. Then McGee put them on his new Warners imprint in the same month Warners released Prince.

eras.title: Named from the first page of Tropic of Cancer
eras.text: After The Loft split, Pete Astor and Dave Morgan started over almost at once. The first singles picked up where the Loft had stopped, and the critics who liked the Loft liked these too.

years.cap: The Weather Prophets at the Tropic Club, Bristol, January 1986
years.src: Wikipedia: The Weather Prophets · WriteWyattUK · Pete Astor: The Weather Prophets
years.h: Alan McGee plays bass, then goes back to managing
years.p: Astor and Morgan name the band after a line in the opening paragraph of Henry Miller's Tropic of Cancer. Greenwood Goulding takes over bass and Oisin Little joins on guitar.
years.xp:
[[Alan McGee|ffacc13a-01e5-4b5d-a455-6a7f302ac9ce]], who ran Creation Records, played bass in the earliest version of the band before stepping back to manage it. Astor has said of McGee: "He was very smart, an incredibly quick learner."

This time Astor came in with "all the songs and a very particular vision about how they should sound." The model was Creedence Clearwater Revival, "an English version of what they did," and later The Lovin' Spoonful.

The four got on well. They had a code for escaping a dull conversation: ask another member whether 'Gerald' was there.

years.src: Discogs: Almost Prayed · Wikipedia: The Weather Prophets
yt: Almost Prayed on The Old Grey Whistle Test, December 1985
years.h: The first single is a Radio 1 session take
years.p: 'Almost Prayed', CRE 029, uses a version recorded at Maida Vale for Janice Long's show, produced by Barry Andrews. Astor produced the B-side at Alaska Studios.

years.cap: Astor on stage at the Tropic Club, Bristol, January 1986
years.h: Patti Smith's guitarist produces 'Naked as the Day You Were Born'
years.p: [[Lenny Kaye|47455aa4-c71e-4662-a775-33b81fcf0a37]] takes the A-side of the second Creation single, CRE 031. Astor produces the B-side, 'In My Room'.
play: Naked as the Day You Were Born
Naked as the Day You Were Born

years.src: Discogs: Diesel River · Wikipedia: The Weather Prophets
years.p: The mini-album on [[Rough Trade|4f4b0013-1704-4936-a769-e6e8a6e08ff8]]'s German arm collects the singles and adds Robert Johnson's 'Stones in My Passway' and Chuck Berry's 'Downbound Train'.

eras.title: Warners' busy month
eras.text: McGee set up Elevation with WEA to get Creation acts into the big shops, and the Weather Prophets were its lead act. The album came out into the wrong crowd.

years.big: Up against Prince, Fleetwood Mac and Simply Red
years.src: Wikipedia: The Weather Prophets · Discogs: Mayflower · Wikipedia: Elevation Records · Raven Sings the Blues · Trouser Press · WriteWyattUK
years.h: Mayflower lands in April with Lenny Kaye producing
years.p: Elevation ELV 1 is cut at Livingston Studios and reaches No. 67 in the UK, to mixed reviews.
years.xp:
"A busy month for Warners," McGee wrote in Creation Stories. The three acts were all at the height of their fame. Mayflower was the first release on Elevation.

Trouser Press's Ira Robbins said Kaye's production "put some starch in the Prophets' sound" while keeping it light. The record re-cuts the Loft's 'Why Does the Rain' and both 1986 singles; Andy Strickland, Astor's old Loft bandmate, has said it frustrated him that they kept re-releasing 'Why Does the Rain'.

yt: She Comes from the Rain, promo video, 1987
years.h: 'She Comes from the Rain' reaches No. 62
years.p: The Mayflower single is the band's highest chart placing in the UK. A new version of 'Why Does the Rain' follows as a 12-inch.

years.src: Wikipedia: Elevation Records · Wikipedia: The Weather Prophets
yt: Live at Surrey University, Guildford, March 1987
years.h: WEA drops the band; McGee calls Elevation his biggest mistake
years.p: The Elevation deal falls apart on poor sales. McGee later said WEA "expected instant hits."

eras.title: Back on Creation, with strings
eras.text: The band went home to Creation and made a second album without Oisin Little. Astor produced it himself, with cello, violin, sax and melodica in the room.

years.src: Discogs: Judges, Juries · Wikipedia: The Weather Prophets · Trouser Press
years.h: Astor produces Judges, Juries and Horsemen himself
years.p: Cut with Pat Collier at the Greenhouse in London between December 1987 and February 1988, CRELP 33 has Little back only as a guest. Early copies come with a free 7-inch.
years.xp:
Goulding plays bass and keyboards. Moira Brown (cello), Verity Clark (viola), Melissa Round (violin), Oscar Morse (sax) and Eddie Saunders (melodica) fill out the sound.

The bonus single pairs 'Odds and Ends' with 'Stepping Lightly on the Ancient Path'.

Trouser Press wasn't won over, calling it "a meandering and uninvolving indulgence in need of clear direction," with a few exceptions.

years.h: 'Always the Light' is the last single, and the band calls it off
years.p: After one more single from Judges, Juries and Horsemen, Astor, Morgan and Goulding end the band.

eras.title: Best mistakes and a band called the Rockingbirds
eras.text: Creation emptied the vaults, Astor went solo, and the rhythm section went country. The songs kept turning up in other people's sets, including the Loft's.

years.p: That's how CRELP 50 bills itself. Six tracks come from a summer 1986 Radio 1 session produced by Barry Andrews and Clive Gregson.
years.xp: Trouser Press rated it "as enjoyable as either of the band's proper albums."

years.src: Wikipedia: Pete Astor · Wikipedia: The Rockingbirds
years.h: Astor's Submarine, and Goulding and Morgan start the Rockingbirds
years.p: Astor's solo debut comes out on Creation. Goulding and Morgan form The Rockingbirds in London, soon signed to Heavenly Recordings.
years.xp:
The Rockingbirds' first Heavenly single was 1991's 'A Good Day for You Is a Good Day for Me', and a tribute to [[Jonathan Richman|bae34b81-9abd-416e-a720-fedc359df775]], 'Jonathan, Jonathan', followed in 1992.

Astor later recorded as the Wisdom of Harry and Ellis Island Sound and became a senior lecturer in music at the University of Westminster.

years.p: A live record from the Mayflower year follows three years after the split.
The best-of brings the Creation and Elevation records back into print together.

years.h: The re-formed Loft play two Weather Prophets songs in Brooklyn
years.p: At NYC Popfest, Astor's first band works 'Joe Shmo & the Eskimo' and 'Can't Keep My Mind Off You' into its set, with Morgan on drums.
